headline: BBC Verify authenticates footage showing Aramco Tower damage far worse than Saudi Arabia's 'minor damage' account'
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the authentication] Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the Aramco Tower than the Saudi Energy Ministry's account: at least one floor appears to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike, and windows on more than one level appear shattered.…
sources: BBC News -- 'Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Ansar Allah launch fresh strikes' (BBC Verify authentication); corroborated by Wall Street Journal, Reuters (via Jerusalem Post), AFP witnesses (via Dawn/Malay Mail)
fault_line: Did Saudi Arabia downplay a direct hit on its oil giant's tower -- 'minor shrapnel damage' or a missile that tore through whole floors?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the authentication] Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the Aramco Tower than the Saudi Energy Ministry's account: at least one floor appears to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike, and windows on more than one level appear shattered. [VERIFIED FACT -- the hit] A projectile hit the Aramco Tower (36-storey 'Villas in the Sky') in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Sunday Nov 8 in a Ansar Allah drone-and-missile attack; the building, which also contains residential units, was empty at the time and no one was killed or injured (WSJ, regional officials). [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] The Ansar Allah claimed responsibility, saying the attack caused significant damage; their Saba news agency statement said they targeted Riyadh's business district without naming the Aramco Tower by name. The group also claimed separate strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco oil storage facilities. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM] The Saudi Energy Ministry said the building suffered only 'minor damage' from 'falling shrapnel' after an 'attempted attack'; the Saudi-led coalition said air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh plus two cruise missiles over Riyadh and the southern region. The strike itself was recorded Nov 8 at totw-20261108-1400-01 (ministry confirmation + Reuters witness of blown-out windows across several floors); the BBC Verify authentication is the NEW element and was recorded in NO Nov 8 or Nov 9 scan (grep: 'BBC Verify' 0 hits in both files).
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: BBC T2 (the verification itself), Wall Street Journal T2 (projectile hit + damage via regional officials), Reuters T1 (via Jerusalem Post carry: windows blown out across several floors), AFP T1 (eyewitnesses via Dawn/Malay Mail: 'Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that's the sure thing'; multiple floors damaged). Attribution-only (NOT counted, no declared tier): New York Post, Daily Caller, GTV News HD, journalarta, vimidi (all carry the BBC Verify line).
sections.what_disputed: Saudi Energy Ministry: only 'minor damage' from 'falling shrapnel', no casualties; coalition interception claims; the Ansar Allah did not name the Aramco Tower in their Saba statement. The ministry did not say where the building was or what struck it. No Aramco comment.
sections.why_matters: Claim-bust: the video vs the official line -- BBC Verify authenticated the damage Riyadh called 'minor'. Hard numbers: at least one floor badly hit, windows blown out across several floors, zero casualties. Proven lane (Ansar Allah strikes on Saudi/Aramco).

totw_analysis: Our read: Claim-bust: the video vs the official line -- BBC Verify authenticated the damage Riyadh called 'minor'. Hard numbers: at least one floor badly hit, windows blown out across several floors, zero casualties. Proven lane (Ansar Allah strikes on Saudi/Aramco). The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did Saudi Arabia downplay a direct hit on its oil giant's tower -- 'minor shrapnel damage' or a missile that tore through whole floors?
